narrative.overview:
RestoFlow is an operations suite dressed as hospitality: the mental model is the kitchen pass during service — dockets line up, timers tick, statuses flip — but the surfaces stay warm and porcelain-clean instead of industrial gray. Every screen is built to be read in one glance under pressure: a status triplet (icon + label + color), tabular numbers that never jitter, and one ember accent that always means "act here". The system refuses dashboard-sterile coldness and equally refuses restaurant-cliché decoration (no food photography, no script fonts, no gingham): warmth comes from color temperature and rounded, tactile geometry, not ornament.

Density is operational but humane — staff screens (kitchen, cashier, admin) pack more per viewport with sticky chrome and multi-column grids; customer screens stay airy, single-column, and thumb-first. Depth is almost flat at rest: thin slate borders and a whisper of two-layer offset shadow, with lift reserved for hover and the floating cart bar. Motion is one authored moment — a soft decelerating rise — so live data updates feel alive without becoming a casino.
keyCharacteristics: One ember accent (#ea580c) for primary action and "your table is occupied"
Status is never color alone: icon + label + color, always, everywhere
Tabular numerals on every price, timer, and quantity
Pill geometry for anything tappable; gently rounded rects (11.2px) for surfaces
Warm porcelain canvas (#f8fafc), white cards, thin slate borders (#e2e8f0)
Plus Jakarta Sans headings against Inter body — confident, not corporate

rules.name: The Status Triplet Rule
rules.body: A status may never be communicated by color alone. Every status indicator ships as icon + text label + color, on light or dark surface, in every role's view.

rules.name: The Ember Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Hearth Ember marks action or your own occupancy — never a decorative background, never a large fill, never body text. If a screen looks orange, something on it is asking to be tapped.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number a user compares across rows or watches tick — prices, timers, quantities, stock, seat counts — renders with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums (the tnum utility). Proportional digits are only for prose.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow as decoration. At rest a card is separated by border and tone; shadow appears only under hover, overlay, or a genuinely floating element.

dos: **Do** pair every status color with an icon and a text label (Status Triplet).
**Do** use `tnum` tabular figures for prices, timers, quantities, stock, and seat counts.
**Do** keep primary actions in Hearth Ember pills and everything tappable in pill geometry.
**Do** separate surfaces with porcelain-vs-white tone plus a 1px `#e2e8f0` border before reaching for shadow.
**Do** keep customer screens in the centered `max-w-lg` column and staff screens in their role's grid (kitchen 4-col, cashier 1fr+400px, admin sidebar).
**Do** set headings in Plus Jakarta Sans at 800 and body in Inter at 14px.
donts: **Don't** communicate state with color alone — no bare colored dots or fills standing in for a status.
**Don't** spend Hearth Ember on decoration: no orange page backgrounds, orange body text, or orange separators.
**Don't** use proportional numerals in tables, timers, or price columns.
**Don't** add shadows at rest, glows on ordinary cards, or a second accent gradient — the ember float is the only glowing treatment.
**Don't** introduce food photography, script display faces, or ornamental textures; the warmth comes from temperature, type, and geometry.
**Don't** shrink hit targets below 32px or truncate a status label — let the row wrap instead.
